newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down in dull trading on Tuesday, with most investors remaining on the sidelines due to uncertainty about the market direction, brokers said.
The index fell 0.075 points or 0.15 percent to 51.018 points, on volume of 5.9 million shares worth $2.7 million. Of 41 B shares, 37 traded, with 13 down, 12 up and 12 flat.
Brokers said investors were cautious about building positions on the lack of a clear market direction.

"Rumors that Shenzhen has begun to restrict domestic investors from buying B stocks depressed market sentiment," one broker said. "But several institutions were buying selective shares when the index fell below 51 points."
"Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development will dominate the market trend in the next few days," a second broker said. "Local and foreign institutions are mixed on its prospects."
Shanghai Lujiazui traded the most, slipping $0.008 or 0.86 percent to $0.922 on volume of 850,800 shares.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation was the biggest loser, falling $0.014 or 7.44 percent to $0.174 on volume of 100,000 shares.
Shanghai A share index closed down sharply on news that 32 firms which sold shares several years ago without central government approval would be permitted to list their shares, brokers said.
The A index ended down 31.307 points or 3.77 percent to 798.471 points, on volume of 316.7 million shares worth 2.9 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 fell 85.348 points or 3.98 percent to 2060.237 points.
Newcomer Huibei Xingfu was the worst performer after over-speculation on Monday, plunging 2.90 yuan or 17.57 percent to 13.60 yuan, on volume of 6.0 million shares.
